coverage.role_matrix: WAREHOUSE vs CLERK/OWNER on read endpoints
coverage.write_endpoints: schema-valid body + non-existent id (no DB writes)
coverage.tenant_isolation: T2 token against T1 object, query-string and header override
coverage.identity_binding: role/user_id/tenant_id query parameters and X-* headers ignored

not_covered: browser-captured HAR (this pack is API-level only)
page-level absence of write entry points (C01 covers this for one DO)
boundaries: Deployed production backend; deployed commit is not exposed by the API.
No DB writes, no reset; /ai/wake is rejected with 403 before any warm-up job.
notes: Warehouse DO is an exact four-key projection; the CLERK projection of the same DO exposes 11 additional top-level fields and 5 additional line fields, all absent from the warehouse body (projection-diff.json).
/ai/status is readable by WAREHOUSE by contract (OpenAPI declares only 200/401) and exposes no business fields; this is not a C08 defect.

Invalid request bodies return 422 before the handler-level role check. The matrix therefore uses schema-valid bodies plus non-existent ids, so a missing guard could only reach 404 and never mutate data.

The implementation also guards /discard and /clarification-copied for WAREHOUSE even though those paths are not in the frozen Gate 0 OpenAPI path set (contract completeness is tracked separately, not as a C08 permission defect).
